reader.requirement: A SAME SORT AREA or SAME SORT-MERGE AREA clause must name at least one sort or merge file (refused otherwise); it may let the named sort and merge files reuse one sort memory area and may lend the named plain files' storage to sorting (extent implementor-specified), but the named plain files must keep distinct record areas from each other (c), every SORT and MERGE must still give its correct result, and the program must not have a named plain file open during a SORT or MERGE of a named sort file (d, a constraint on the program with no stated outcome).

edition-consulted.switches: report-file row only (below 2002 a report file may appear in SAME SORT/SORT-MERGE AREA clauses); sort-merge and plain rows identical
held1985: two SORT GIVING files in one SAME RECORD AREA clause refused below 2002 (XI.4.4.3 SR9); the SAME SORT/SORT-MERGE AREA pair rule is the same arm at every edition

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for GR2's storage semantics: the sort-merge-area format creates no storage sharing at any edition (the documented extent is none, docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-169.md); the edition arms on the path touch report files and SORT GIVING files only

reader.notes: The sort-merge-area format records membership only (FileModel.SameClauses) and links no storage; LinkSameRecordArea runs only for SAME RECORD AREA, so plain files named together never alias, and SORT/MERGE work storage is the runtime's own. Side observation, not this rule: when a SORT is refused (COBOL1757), the RELEASE/RETURN in its procedures get COBOL7081 cascades (p2d, p2e), which may mislead a reader into a second fault.
